title: CGM LED Matrix configuration
description: Settings read by GlucosePixelMatrix.py at startup. The display service must be restarted for changes to take effect. Keys starting with x- are UI hints for the web configurator and are ignored by validators.

x-groups.title: Nightscout
x-groups.description: Where the glucose readings, treatments and insulin on board come from.

x-groups.title: Display
x-groups.description: The iDotMatrix panel and how the app talks to it over Bluetooth.

x-groups.title: Glucose range
x-groups.description: Your target range. It draws the two guide lines and decides the colors: green inside, yellow at the edges, red more than 10 mg/dL outside.

x-groups.title: Clock
x-groups.description: An optional clock drawn over the graph. It is always shown while the data is stale, so you can see how old it is.

x-groups.title: Night mode & alerts
x-groups.description: Brightness from 22:00 to 06:59 (100% during the day) and when old data is flagged.

x-groups.title: Google Calendar
x-groups.description: Keeps one ten-minute event such as “🟢 112 → +2” in a calendar, so the reading shows up on a phone or watch. Needs OAuth credentials, see the README.

url.title: Nightscout API URL
url.description: Your site followed by /api/v2. The app appends /entries.json, /treatments.json and /properties/iob.

token.title: Access token
token.description: A token with read access, created in Nightscout under Admin Tools → Subjects (for example readable-1a2b3c4d5e6f). It is never shown here once saved and never written to the logs.

image out.title: Output
image out.description: Send each frame to the LED matrix over Bluetooth, or only render it to temp/output_image.png (useful for testing on a computer; the preview on this page still works).

ip.title: Display Bluetooth address
ip.description: The MAC address of the panel; its Bluetooth name starts with IDM-. Find it with: python -c "import asyncio; from idotmatrix import ConnectionManager; print(asyncio.run(ConnectionManager.scan()))"

os.title: Operating system
os.description: On Linux the app runs rfkill unblock bluetooth at startup. Pick the system the display service runs on.

plot glucose intervals.title: Connect readings with lines
plot glucose intervals.description: Draw faint lines between consecutive readings so the trend is easier to follow.

low boundary glucose.title: Low limit
low boundary glucose.description: Readings at or below this turn yellow, and red below it minus 10.

high boundary glucose.title: High limit
high boundary glucose.description: Readings at or above this turn yellow, and red above it plus 10.

show_time.title: Show the clock
show_time.description: Draw the current time; the frame is redrawn every minute to keep it current.

time_format.title: Format
time_format.description: Seconds are only updated once a minute, so the formats with seconds are rarely useful.

time_position.title: Position
time_position.description: Top positions sit just under the high limit line, bottom ones near the low limit.

night_brightness.title: Night brightness
night_brightness.description: Applied from 22:00 to 06:59; daytime is always 100%. Older configs with a fraction such as 0.1 are read as 10%.

stale_minutes.title: Flag data as stale after
stale_minutes.description: With no new reading for this long, a red mark replaces the reading-age counter and the clock is shown.

google_calendar_enabled.title: Sync the reading to Google Calendar
google_calendar_enabled.description: On the first run a browser window asks you to authorize access, so authorize once on a computer and copy the token file to the Pi.

google_calendar_id.title: Calendar
google_calendar_id.description: The calendar's name (for example cgm) or primary for your main calendar. Its events are replaced on every reading, so use a dedicated calendar.

google_calendar_credentials.title: OAuth credentials file
google_calendar_credentials.description: The Desktop-app client JSON downloaded from Google Cloud. Relative paths are resolved from the project folder.

google_calendar_token.title: Token file
google_calendar_token.description: Where the authorization is stored after the first login. Created automatically.

time_color_fade.description: Not used yet: the clock is always drawn at full brightness.

PIXEL_INTERVAL.description: Not used yet: each column is always five minutes.

output type.description: Deprecated and ignored: the display always receives an image. Kept so older configs still validate.
